Most large-scale psychometric studies have found that while average IQ scores do show statistically significant differences across racial groups, these gaps largely disappear when researchers meticulously control for parental education, income, and nutrition—factors completely separable from genetics. Even when such controls are unavailable in older datasets, most modern experts caution that these raw score differences arise more from environmental disadvantages like lead exposure or discriminatory educational access than from inherent cognitive potential, stemming primarily from decades of sociological consensus.
